title: Chunked Claude-CLI labeling for >50 patches
description:
After PATCH-8, label-patches produces 98+ anatomical patches on the skull and Claude CLI times out at 600s processing the single-shot prompt plus two images. Decomposer is correct; only the semantic-naming step stalls.

Options to implement (pick one during the ticket):

1. Chunked labeling (preferred): split patches into batches of 30-40 by decomposition order, call claude -p once per batch, merge mapping results. Total time scales linearly with batch count but each call stays well under timeout.

2. Top-N pre-filter: sort patches by vertex count, keep top 40, rest stay placeholders. Covers anatomically important patches. Simplest but loses small-patch labels.

3. Streaming + resume: use claude -p --output-format stream-json to see progress, allow partial completion. Most robust.

Recommendation: start with (1) batched, fall back to (2) if batching complicates merge logic.

Additional: the prompt should be reorganized so Claude sees the two renders first and the patch list second, so reasoning about image content precedes the mapping decision.
definition-of-done: uv run label-patches on the current skull produces a tags.json with all patches either semantically labeled or explicitly marked as placeholder, no timeouts, completes in under 10 minutes.
testing-plan: Run label-patches on /tmp/skull.obj with the PATCH-8 decomposer output (98 patches). Verify completion, verify labels are anatomically sensible, verify no patch is silently dropped.
